hints.title: Rolling 300-Second Request Counting
hints.text: The counter records discrete events over time and answers queries for the total hits received within the preceding 300 seconds.

hints.title: Circular Buffer or Rolling Deque
hints.text: Because the observation window is fixed at 300 seconds, store counts across 300 discrete seconds using modulo indexing or purge expired hits.

hints.title: Fixed Array Bucket Blueprint
hints.text: Allocate times = [0] * 300 and hits = [0] * 300. Index is timestamp % 300. In hit(): when times[idx] differs from timestamp, update times[idx] = timestamp and hits[idx] = 1; else increment hits[idx]. In getHits(): sum hits[i] where timestamp - times[i] < 300.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(1) hit, O(B) getHits where B = 300
variables: B: 300 bucket seconds in circular buffer
complexity.notes: Constant space circular array handles arbitrary volume of concurrent requests.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing every individual hit timestamp in an unbounded list exhausts memory under millions of hits per second.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fixed 300-slot circular array achieves constant O(1) space bound regardless of hit volume.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining concurrency resilience and memory bounds with circular bucket design.
